title: FR-01 Interactive prompt and read-eval loop
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want interactive prompt and read-eval loop, so that I can type commands and see results one after another.

**Requirement:** FR-01 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Command Loop and Input Sources  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-1 / DES-03, DES-06  
**Source files:** shell.c, parser.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] When standard input is a terminal the shell shall display a prompt containing the current working directory, read one line, execute it, and repeat until told to exit.
- [ ] Behaviour: Prompt has the form mysh:<cwd>$ and is written to stderr. Blank, whitespace-only and comment-only lines are accepted and do nothing (status unchanged).
- [ ] Errors: If getcwd() fails the prompt falls back to mysh$ . A failed read caused by a signal redraws the prompt (see FR-21).

**Tests that must pass:** TC-47, UT-18  
**System tests:** ST-01, ST-02, ST-10

**Story points:** 5  
**Sprint:** Sprint 1  
**Owner (documented in Part-1 ownership table):** Member 1  
**Priority:** high

title: FR-02 Non-interactive input sources
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want non-interactive input sources, so that I can automate commands from a script, a string or a pipe.

**Requirement:** FR-02 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Command Loop and Input Sources  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-1 / DES-01, DES-03  
**Source files:** main.c, shell.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The shell shall accept commands from (a) a terminal, (b) standard input when it is not a terminal, (c) a script file argument, and (d) a command string given with -c. --help and --version shall print information and exit.
- [ ] Behaviour: No prompt is printed and no job banners are shown in non-interactive modes. The exit status is the status of the last command, or the value given to exit.
- [ ] Errors: -c without an argument prints a usage message and exits with status 2. An unreadable script file prints an error and exits with status 127.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-50, TC-51, TC-62, TC-63, TC-76  
**System tests:** ST-10

**Story points:** 3  
**Sprint:** Sprint 1

title: FR-03 Tokenization and quoting
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want tokenization and quoting, so that arguments with spaces, quotes and operators are understood correctly.

**Requirement:** FR-03 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Command-Line Parsing  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-2 / DES-06, DES-07  
**Source files:** parser.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The parser shall split a line into words separated by blanks; single quotes shall preserve text literally, double quotes shall preserve blanks and operators but allow expansion, a backslash shall escape the next character, and text after an unquoted # at the start of a word shall be a comment.
- [ ] Behaviour: Operators | < > >> ; & are recognised without surrounding spaces (echo x>f). Quoted operators are ordinary text.
- [ ] Errors: Unterminated quotes are syntax errors (FR-04).

**Tests that must pass:** TC-37, TC-39, TC-40, UT-01, UT-02, UT-05, UT-06  
**System tests:** ST-10

**Story points:** 8

title: FR-04 Syntax error detection and reporting
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want syntax error detection and reporting, so that mistakes in my command line are explained instead of crashing the shell.

**Requirement:** FR-04 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Command-Line Parsing  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-2 / DES-06, DES-04  
**Source files:** parser.c, shell.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The parser shall detect and report: unterminated single or double quotes, a redirection operator with no file name, an empty pipeline stage (leading, trailing or doubled |), a redirection with no command, a malformed ${...}, and the unsupported operators && and ||.
- [ ] Behaviour: A message of the form 'mysh: <reason>' is written to stderr, $? is set to 2, and the remainder of the input line is discarded. The shell continues with the next line.
- [ ] Errors: No command from the faulty pipeline is executed. The shell never terminates because of a syntax error.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-41, TC-42, TC-43, TC-44, TC-45, TC-46, TC-70, TC-73, UT-12, UT-13, UT-14, UT-15, UT-16, UT-22, UT-23  
**System tests:** ST-10

title: FR-05 External command execution with PATH search
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want external command execution with PATH search, so that I can run any installed program.

**Requirement:** FR-05 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** External Command Execution  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-3 / DES-09, DES-10  
**Source files:** executor.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] For a command that is not a built-in the shell shall create a child process with fork() and replace it with the program using execvp(), searching the directories in PATH when the name contains no slash.
- [ ] Behaviour: Arguments are passed unchanged (after quote removal and expansion) as argv. A name containing / is used as a path and is not searched in PATH.
- [ ] Errors: See FR-07 for exec failures. If fork() or pipe() fails, already-started children are reaped, an error is printed and the status is 1.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-02, TC-03, TC-10, TC-48, TC-49  
**System tests:** ST-02, ST-10

title: FR-06 Foreground wait and exit status
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want foreground wait and exit status, so that commands finish before the next prompt and I can check their status.

**Requirement:** FR-06 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** External Command Execution  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-3 / DES-12  
**Source files:** executor.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The shell shall wait for every foreground child before reading the next command and shall record the exit status of the last command of a pipeline in $?.
- [ ] Behaviour: Normal exit -> exit code. Death by signal N -> 128+N and a message (strsignal) on stderr, except SIGINT (newline only) and SIGPIPE (silent).
- [ ] Errors: waitpid() interrupted by a signal is retried.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-30, TC-56  
**System tests:** ST-04, ST-10

**Story points:** 3

title: FR-07 Invalid command handling
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want invalid command handling, so that I know when a command does not exist or cannot be run.

**Source files:** executor.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] When a command cannot be executed the shell shall print a diagnostic, set the status and continue.
- [ ] Behaviour: Name not found in PATH -> 'mysh: <name>: command not found', status 127. Path with / not found -> 'No such file or directory', status 127. Found but not executable (e.g. EACCES) -> strerror message, status 126.
- [ ] Errors: The child exits; the shell prompts again.

title: FR-08 Built-in cd
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want built-in cd, so that I can move around the directory tree.

**Requirement:** FR-08 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Built-in Commands  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-4 / DES-14, DES-15  
**Source files:** builtins.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] cd [dir] shall change the working directory of the shell process itself; cd with no argument shall use $HOME; cd - shall return to $OLDPWD and print the new directory. PWD and OLDPWD shall be updated.
- [ ] Behaviour: Runs in the shell process (not a child) so the change persists.
- [ ] Errors: Missing/inaccessible directory -> 'cd: <dir>: <strerror>', status 1. More than one argument -> 'too many arguments', status 1. HOME or OLDPWD unset when needed -> error, status 1.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-04, TC-05, TC-06, TC-07, TC-65

title: FR-10 Built-in exit
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want built-in exit, so that I can leave the shell with a chosen status.

**Requirement:** FR-10 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Built-in Commands  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-4 / DES-14, DES-17  
**Source files:** builtins.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] exit [n] shall terminate the shell with status n (0-255, taken modulo 256), or with the status of the last command when n is omitted. Remaining input is not executed.
- [ ] Behaviour: Background jobs are not signalled; they are left running.
- [ ] Errors: Non-numeric argument -> 'exit: <arg>: numeric argument required' and the shell exits with status 2. More than one argument -> error, shell does not exit, status 1.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-31, TC-32, TC-33, TC-53

body:
**Story**

As a user, I want background execution with &, so that I can keep working while a long job runs.

**Requirement:** FR-20 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Background Execution  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-3 / DES-09, DES-13  
**Source files:** executor.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A pipeline terminated by & shall be started and the shell shall immediately continue without waiting. Interactively the shell prints [id] pid on start and [id]+ Done <command> when it has finished (reported before the next prompt).
- [ ] Behaviour: Background processes read from /dev/null unless redirected, ignore SIGINT, and are reaped with waitpid(WNOHANG) so they do not remain zombies. Status of the & pipeline is 0.
- [ ] Errors: If the job table (64 entries) is full the job still runs but is not reported.

**Tests that must pass:** TC-36, TC-74, TC-75, UT-10

title: FR-21 Signal handling
body:
**Story**

As a user, I want signal handling, so that Ctrl+C stops a runaway job without closing my shell.

**Requirement:** FR-21 (see `docs/SRS.docx` and `docs/RTM.md`)  
**Epic:** Signal Handling  
**Architecture / design refs:** ARCH-6 / DES-05, DES-10, DES-12  
**Source files:** shell.c, executor.c

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] In interactive mode Ctrl+C shall interrupt the current input line or foreground job without terminating the shell; Ctrl+\ and Ctrl+Z shall not stop or kill the shell or its foreground jobs (no job control).
- [ ] Behaviour: At the prompt Ctrl+C abandons the line, prints a newline, sets $? to 130 and redraws the prompt. A foreground child receives the default SIGINT action; the shell reports status 130. Background jobs are not affected by Ctrl+C.
- [ ] Errors: SIGPIPE keeps its default action in children.

**Tests that must pass:** -  
**System tests:** ST-03, ST-04, ST-07, ST-08, ST-10, ST-11
